svg.aria-label: How an incident becomes a test, in six steps. 1 Incident: a labelled GitHub issue, a pasted postmortem, a form, or an alert from Sentry, PagerDuty and more in Labs. 2 Draft: a model drafts one test in the repository's framework and style. 3 Fails before the fix: it runs three times on the commit before the fix and must fail every time; if it passes, it is redrafted with the failure as feedback, up to 3 times. 4 Passes on the fix: it runs three times on the fix and must pass every time; then it is proven. 5 Memory: the proven test lands by pull request and re-runs every night on main, marked Healthy, Flaky or Failing. 6 Guards every PR: each pull request runs the relevant tests and gets one check and one comment: Recur, Safe, Inconclusive or Skipped. Every run is a fresh microVM with no network and no secrets. A model never marks anything proven or safe; only test runs do.

g.text: HOW AN INCIDENT BECOMES A TEST
EVERY RUN: A FRESH MICROVM / NO NETWORK / NO SECRETS
A labelled GitHub issue, a pasted
postmortem, a form or an alert.
Run three times on the fix.
It must pass every time. Then it is proven.
A model drafts one test in your
PYTEST / VITEST / JEST / MORE IN LABS
The proven test lands by pull request
and re-runs every night on main.
Run three times on the commit
before the fix. It must fail every time.
Each pull request runs the relevant tests:
admitted only if it fails 3/3 before the fix and passes 3/3 on it
passed before the fix? redraft with the failure, up to 3 times
A model never marks anything proven or safe; only test runs do. Mixed results are never green.
